bug_semantics: The POST routes /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events accepted a caller-controlled HTTPS MISP base URL and made server-side requests whose response data was returned to the caller. _validate_misp_url rejected unsafe IP literals but accepted every ordinary hostname without resolving it, so an attacker could use a hostname resolving to a private, loopback, link-local, or reserved address to reach and read an internal HTTPS service. The routes were also callable anonymously, increasing exposure, while the unresolved-hostname allow decision was the SSRF root cause.
flaw_origin: Commit b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 directly added website/web/convert/convert.py::_validate_misp_url and both outbound-request routes. Its ValueError branch used `pass  # it's a domain name — OK`, accepting non-IP hostnames without checking resolved destinations. The same direct feature commit added the unauthenticated request sinks; it was not an import, move, refactor, revert, release commit, or decomposed squash member.
ai_marker: absent — BIC commit object has no AI author/co-author/Generated-with marker; see evidence
evidence: The published GitHub advisory GHSA-x373-32xc-7gqv / CVE-2026-73160 names SSRF in /fetch_misp_event and /misp_search_events, explains that ordinary hostnames were accepted without DNS resolution, states that anonymous callers could make the server request an internal target and read the response, and references direct fix 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512. It lists affected and patched versions as Unknown.

`git diff --unified=2 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5 b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 -- website/web/convert/convert.py` shows the validator, its unsafe `except ValueError: pass` branch, and both unauthenticated request/response routes as additions against the immediate parent. `git cat-file -p b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` confirms that 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5 is the sole direct parent. Thus the mechanism is absent from the parent rather than imported or moved there.

`git log --all -S"pass  # it's a domain name — OK" --format='%H %P %s' --name-status --` returns b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 as the addition and 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 as the removal. This pickaxe result, together with the direct parent diff, establishes the smallest real BIC and rejects later path renames or refactors as origin candidates.

`git diff --unified=2 957c56bdc64bfbbf9fafacc9a410dcbf32371cfd 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 -- website/web/conversions/conversions.py` shows the direct fix adding socket.getaddrinfo resolution, requiring every resolved address to be global, and adding @login_required to both affected routes. `git show --format=fuller --stat --summary 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512` shows one parent, 957c56bdc64bfbbf9fafacc9a410dcbf32371cfd, and a one-file security fix, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha coincide.

Version-boundary checks: `git tag --contains b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` returns v1.3, v1.4, and v1.5; `git tag --contains 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512` returns only v1.5. Chronological `git for-each-ref` output places v1.2 before the BIC, v1.3 and v1.4 after the BIC but before the fix, and v1.5 after the fix. The repository boundary is therefore first affected v1.3, still affected v1.4, first fixed v1.5, despite the advisory's Unknown version fields.

Disagreement marker_state: the primary encoded a prose string saying the marker was absent, while the reviewer encoded `ai_marker` as null. The re-run `git cat-file -p b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48` shows only tree, sole parent 4637cf8255487759ba648cff7e374d7c995468a5, author and committer `ecrou-exact <geffetheo@gmail.com>`, and subject `add: [misp connection] can connect to a misp instance and select event to import`; there is no body, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other AI marker. Therefore the reviewer wins the canonical marker state (`ai_marker`: null), although the primary's underlying observation of absence was substantively correct. No later commit or PR signal is used.
reasoning: The vulnerable mechanism first exists in b9f40af30de83fa44a14a3b0263df26192696b48 because that one-parent source commit jointly adds the destination guard that trusts unresolved hostnames and the two request sinks that return remote data; the direct parent has none of those additions, and pickaxe history identifies no earlier source origin. The advisory's referenced commit 4d29109a6f185d5e7c7f3b906f822ab34403f512 directly repairs the same trust decision and protects both routes, with its parent still carrying the vulnerable line. Tag containment establishes v1.3-v1.4 as vulnerable and v1.5 as fixed. The only primary/reviewer disagreement is marker_state: both audits found no BIC commit-object AI evidence, but the primary put an explanatory absence sentence into ai_marker whereas the reviewer used null. Reinspection of the raw BIC object finds no marker payload to record, so null is the resolved canonical value and the reviewer wins that field. Because attribution is restricted to the BIC commit object, the absence of an AI marker yields NOT_AI.
